text:
ana (PM): Quick planning thread — we need a tenant-aware A/B rollout plan for the new routing policy (weight-based fallbacks + regional holdbacks). Goals: minimize user-visible regressions, keep p95 latency under 400ms, and allow fast rollback for top-tier customers.

mike (eng): +1. rough sketch: 5% global sample -> staggered region canaries (US-EAST, EU-WEST, AP-SE) -> 20% tenant buckets -> expand. each stage has an automated rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or p95 > 500ms for 5m.

ana (PM): typo: that should be 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline, not raw error rate. also need quality guardrails (generation regressions). olivia, can we tie this to the evaluation prompt set?

olivia (product-analytics): yes — we'll use the smoke prompt set + 500 labeled prompts for automated regression checks. Proposed thresholds: delta_quality_score <= -3 pts AND significant by bootstrap -> trigger alert. We'll also track completions/success-rate for customer flows (login help, search rerank).

devon (sre): Operational constraints: each canary window = 30m with warmup + 30m steady-state. If we hit latency SLO breach, route traffic to fallback variant (current routing) automatically. Need circuit-breaker: if p95 > 450ms for 3 consecutive windows -> full rollback. Also require canary isolation: dedicated instance pool or tagged nodes.

sam (infra): tagging pool is doable. Also recommend a degraded-mode policy: when model or routing variant fails, downgrade to reduced batch size + cached responses before full fallback. That preserves availability for high-traffic tenants.

mike (eng): Implementation details: feature flag schema and assignment. idea: flag keys: "routing.v3.rollout", dimensioned by region and tenant_bucket. Example assignment rule: 
```
{"flag": "routing.v3.rollout", "rules": [{"region": "us-east", "pct": 5}, {"region": "eu-west", "pct": 2}, {"tenant_tier": "enterprise", "pct": 0}]}
```
We should reserve an opt-in path for enterprise tenants (0% by default) and an explicit opt-in override.

ana (PM): Agree on enterprise opt-in. We also need a fast manual kill switch per-customer in the console + API for support->ops. Document the path.

devon (sre): @ana add on-call runbook: 
- who: oncall-sre + eng-service-owner
- action: flip flag to baseline, re-route, confirm backlog drained
- postmortem gating: any customer-facing regression >30min triggers incident.

mike (eng): A/B measurement notes: we should avoid cross-contamination. Use sticky assignment by tenant_id hashing + region seed. Sampling pseudocode: 
```
seed = hash(tenant_id + flag_version + region)
bucket = seed % 100
if bucket < pct -> variant
```
Will implement in routing middleware.

olivia (product-analytics): Analysis plan: run Bayesian lift analysis on primary metrics (success_rate, median_latency, revenue proxy for enterprise). Pre-spec: 24h burn-in, then daily checks. Keep per-tenant dashboards and cohort-level summaries.

ana (PM): Launch gates checklist (minimum to proceed beyond 5%): 
- No significant quality regressions on smoke set (olivia)
- p95 latency delta < 20% vs baseline for canary region (devon)
- Error rate delta < 0.5% absolute (devon)
- Feature flag + kill switch tested in staging (mike/sam)
- Observability dashboards created and alerted (olivia/devon)
- Customer opt-in flows documented (support/solutions)

sam (infra): Can we add a gradual resource cap? e.g., limit routing.v3 to X RPS per region during canary to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Configurable in the flag metadata.

mike (eng): yep — flag metadata can include qos caps. Example: 
```
{"qos": {"max_rps": 2000, "burst": 500}}
```
Routing will enforce via token bucket before sending to variant.

olivia (product-analytics): One more: we should pre-register control tasks to validate drift in embeddings or rerank heuristics. If drift > threshold, auto-hold rollout.

devon (sre): Also add a fallback variant list: primary -> canary -> cached -> baseline. That way we degrade gracefully. Document ordering and TTLs for cached fallback.

ana (PM): Decision items for next week: 
- final sampling percentages per region (mike + olivia)
- exact quality thresholds on eval set (olivia)
- kill-switch API design + console button (sam + mike)
- runbook + SLO triggers (devon)
Would like a go/no-go sync on Thursday.

mike (eng): I'll draft flag JSON + middleware PR. ETA Tue.

sam (infra): I'll add tagged node pool + burst caps in infra template and expose kill-switch endpoint. ETA Wed.

olivia (product-analytics): I'll produce the smoke-runner and initial thresholds, and wire dashboards. ETA Wed morning.

devon (sre): I'll add canary monitors and automatic rollback hooks to the routing controller. ETA Wed afternoon.

deploy-bot: canary scheduled: routing.v3 -> us-east (5%) at 2026-03-24T14:00Z. CI: passed.

ana (PM): Great — add docs links in thread when PRs are up. Also create a small customer comms note for enterprise teams in case they see anomalies.

mike (eng): will do. posting PR link once opened.

olivia (product-analytics): tagging: @devon @sam for dashboards.

devon (sre): noted. will review PRs and add rollback test cases.

ana (PM): Thanks everyone. Quick final: ensure experiment meta includes "exp_owner", "flag_version", "seed" and data retention policy (30d raw, 180d aggregated).

mike (eng): noted — will include retention and opt-out hooks.

sam (infra): added to infra ticket.

ana (PM): closing thread for now — we’ll reconvene on Thursday for go/no-go.
